findings.title: Engine report surface has no tenant dimension; any signed-in org can list, run and download every org's engine reports
findings.description: The cloud routes authenticate the session for organizationId but never use it for scoping; EngineClient has no tenant parameter and one shared token; the engine host keeps a single global markting-reports.json index and serves any artefact to any valid token. Org A's runs (requested_by, windows, platform summaries, files) appear on org B's Reports page and B can download A's HTML/PDF. A global asyncio.Lock serialises all runs while the cloud allows 120 runs/min per org, so one tenant can starve others. Mitigating: the host refuses to boot unless data mode is 'sample', so today the leaked content is synthetic.
findings.recommendation: Store report runs in adport Postgres keyed by organization_id and serve only own rows (or run one engine per tenant / pass an org-scoped caller_ref and partition the engine index and artefact dir per caller). Lower the per-org report rate limit and queue runs instead of a global lock.

findings.title: Assistant is one synchronous HTTP request that may run for minutes; no streaming, no job, no persisted messages
findings.description: maxDuration=300 only informs deployment platforms and does nothing on the standalone Node server; the engine call blocks for up to 240 s (max 900 s) behind any proxy/LB that terminates idle responses. Conversation state lives only in React state; a reload loses it and threadId; listThreads is unused so markting_threads records ownership only. Each in-flight turn pins a request and a DB pool slot.
findings.recommendation: Make engine turns asynchronous (enqueue + poll or SSE stream), persist messages per thread, add cancel, put threadId in the URL for resumption.

findings.title: Bridge throws outside its try/catch when the translated tool is not registered; proposal left dangling on the engine with no record or hand-off

findings.title: Apply is not atomic across concurrent approvers; dashboard scans pending rows O(n) with a hard 200 cap
evidence: platform/apps/cloud/lib/cloud/repository.ts (PostgresPendingStore.get/delete, no FOR UPDATE or conditional consume)
findings.description: Two admins or two tabs clicking Apply within the provider round-trip both pass get(), both call applyWrite, both write an 'applied' audit event. Only idempotent budget/status updates are translated so the platform effect is benign today, but the audit double-counts and a non-idempotent tool would double-apply. listPendingOperations(...,200).find returns 404 for rows beyond 200. markPendingOutcome runs only after success so provenance can stay 'pending' on a consumed row. Upstream engine weakness, newly exposed by a second human-driven surface.
findings.recommendation: Consume first with update ... set consumed_at=now() where id=$1 and consumed_at is null returning * (compensate on provider failure) or select ... for update skip locked; fetch by id; write provenance in the same transaction.

findings.title: Defence-in-depth gaps: unsafe-inline scripts, non-HttpOnly auth cookies, no Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check on cookie-authenticated JSON POSTs

findings.title: jsonb columns asserted into TS types, never parsed (except policy and sandbox state)

findings.title: Four parallel error hierarchies glued by string matching; AdportError codes stretched semantically

POLICY_VIOLATION details include the whole org policy, serialized to MCP callers via toJSON(). No security impact found (REST returns message only; MCP caller is the tenant's own agent).
findings.recommendation: Typed AuthenticationError mapped centrally in apiError; a cloud-side error union (UNAUTHENTICATED/FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/UPSTREAM) instead of overloading core codes; redact `policy` from error details.

findings.title: PolicyEngine.apply has no atomic claim: concurrent applies of one pending id execute the provider write twice
evidence: node d7-double-apply.mjs => exit 0: 'S1 concurrent apply: applyWrite calls = 2 | outcomes = fulfilled, fulfilled | applied audit events = 2'
findings.description: apply() reads the pending row, calls provider.applyWrite, then soft-deletes. The store contract (delete(): void) cannot express a claim and the Postgres delete has no 'consumed_at is null' guard or returning, so every concurrent caller that passes get() executes. For create-kind tools (10 provider packages) this is a duplicate campaign with real spend; for update-kind tools the audit log double-counts.
findings.recommendation: Add claim(id) to PendingOperationStore implemented as a conditional 'update ... where consumed_at is null and expires_at > now() returning *' and call it before applyWrite; or wrap the apply route in a transaction with select ... for update. Add a concurrency test to packages/core.

findings.title: Apply does not re-preview: budget-delta cap and fromMicros baseline are frozen at validate time

findings.recommendation: Re-run previewWrite + checkBudgetPolicy inside apply and fail with PENDING_MISMATCH on material difference.

key_findings: Approved-once is not applied-once: PolicyEngine.apply reads, writes to the provider, then soft-deletes with an unconditional update; a scratch probe against the built core shows two concurrent applies execute applyWrite twice and a post-write audit failure leaves the row consumable so a retry executes again (P1, create-kind tools exist in 10 providers).

The shipped default demo engine is broken past the first conversation: LoopingScriptedChatModel keeps process-global script state, so the next new thread gets the 'exhausted' text and concurrent chats corrupt each other (verified at runtime; existing tests use a fresh app per test and cannot see it).

The chat turn is a minutes-long synchronous HTTP call with no job/queue, no idempotency key, no engine-side timeout, no health gating and no per-thread lock on either side; a timed-out turn loses output and a proposal it produced is bridged only on the user's next message.

The engine host's report index is a plain JSON file written non-atomically; a corrupt read silently returns [] (verified), the single asyncio.Lock serialises every tenant's report run, and PDF rendering runs synchronously on the event loop.

The engine is a single-tenant, single-process SPOF shared by all organizations: one bearer caller, globally visible report runs (fixture data only today, cross-tenant if ever live), in-memory state and a container volume that preclude replicas, and cloud boot coupled to engine health.

Pending TTL (15 min) gates a four-eyes approval with no notification; 'expired' is never recorded so provenance rows stay 'pending' forever; the hand-off already rejected the engine proposal so users must re-chat.
Hand-off to the engine is best-effort and silent; orphan awaiting_approval proposals accumulate (verified) and re-bridging the same proposal can create a second applyable pending row.
Sandbox compare-and-set and the engine's proposal CAS / single-use approval claims are sound; the cloud app itself is stateless and DB-pool-safe during long engine calls.
